SMTO-HTTP-0009 — This run's HTTP connections have already been closed

GUID: cc8d10b7-32b5-4357-ad15-d64155c3507e
Slug: http-connection-expired
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO tried to set up a connection to a service for a run that had already ended, been stopped or been cleaned up, so it refused. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the earlier run was changing something on the service, such as creating or updating a record, check on the service whether that change already happened. The connection closing doesn't prove that an earlier change didn't go through.
  2. Send a new message in the conversation asking SMTO to do only what is still needed. A new run sets up its own fresh connection to the service.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects again in the new run and the request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a request that changes something on the service until you've confirmed whether the first one went through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HttpConnections.capture was called on a run-scoped connection registry that is no longer active (the run finished, was cancelled or abandoned, or its workspace connections were cleared).

What this means

  • Connection capture was attempted through a registry whose active flag is false. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Connection capture was attempted through a registry whose active flag is false.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether the task/run has ended and whether the invocation uses its current registry; this is not a token-expiry diagnosis.

How to fix it

  • Start or resume an active run and call http.connect again to get a new connection_ref; references from an ended run can't be reused. If an earlier write in that run was interrupted, verify its outcome on the target service before repeating it.
  • Reconnect and use the newly returned connection reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported active run establishes its own current connection reference.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
